messages.subject: Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR) - suggested improvements?
parts:
Dear List,

I am working on a hierarchical SUR model and was hoping to get feedback on a
much-simplified version. The Stan SUR model below replicates the results of the
first example shown at the UCLA Stata site (section 4.5.1 -- example R code is
attached, as is a dump file for the data).

Performance for this simple model/dataset is good enough, but when I take the
model to my data (50000+ obs, 9000+ individuals, in up to 7 equations), things 
turn strange (e.g., greater than 48 hours of run time on a high-performance cluster,
very little or no mixing). Now, it's quite possible (even likely) that I have
something wrong in my more complicated model, but I wanted to see if the list
had any comments on this simplified version before I bother you all with the
ugly one. For instance, if my correlation matrices are never more than 7x7, do I
need to go the cholesky route?

Thanks for your time.
~Jason

// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Seemingly Unrelated Regression
// -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

data {
  int<lower=1> N; // number of observations
  int<lower=2> P; // number of equations

  vector[P] x[N]; // first covariate
  vector[P] z[N]; // second covariate
  vector[P] y[N]; // outcomes
}
parameters {
  vector[P] alpha;
  vector[P] beta_x; // first coef.
  vector[P] beta_z; // second coef.

  vector<lower=0>[P] sigma;
  corr_matrix[P] Sigma;
}
model {
  matrix[P,P] Omega;
  Omega <- quad_form_diag(Sigma, sigma);

  sigma ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
  Sigma ~ lkj_corr(2.0);

  alpha  ~ normal(0, 10);
  beta_x ~ normal(0, 10);
  beta_z ~ normal(0, 10);

  {
    vector[P] theta[N];

    for(n in 1:N)
      theta[n] <- alpha + (x[n] .* beta_x) + (z[n] .* beta_z);

    y ~ multi_normal(theta, Omega);
  }
}

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Seemingly Unrelated Regression (SUR) - suggested improvements?
parts:
On Saturday, June 13, 2015 at 10:45:21 AM UTC-4, Jason Morgan wrote:
For instance, if my correlation matrices are never more than 7x7, do I
need to go the cholesky route?

The overhead of correlation matrices that are of order 7 is going to be small relative to the cost (time, memory, imprecision) of autodiffing linear predictors that are 50000 x 7. But there is no advantage to a corr_matrix relative to a cholesky_factor_corr. If you haven't already, I would try centering and possibly rescaling the predictors.

Ben
